LESSON: LENGTH

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: MEASUREMENT
Topic 2.1: Length
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Length, part of MEASUREMENT in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: How do you measure the chalkboard using a metre stick? 2. How do you get the total length in metres of the 4 classroom walls?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign length and terms related to length,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Length in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. measure length using fixed units,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Length in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. identify the metre as a unit of measuring length,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Length in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. measure length in metres,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Length in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate measuring length using fixed units in real life situations. ● Learners in pairs/group are guided to identify, fingerspell, read by signing and write length and terms related to length such as meters, distance, measure, estimate. ● In pairs or groups, use sticks of equal length to measure lengths of different objects and record the measurements. ● In pairs or groups, use sticks of different lengths to measure length, including a 1- metre sticks. ● Use locally available materials to make 1-metre sticks and use them to measure the length of various objects within the classroom and record the measurements. ● Measure the length of different objects at home, record the measurements and discuss with peers in school. ● Learners in pairs are guided to watch and take videos of others measuring length then play back and discuss their results using digital devices. 1. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Length together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: Interacting with digital technology playing games involving length measurement using digital devices,

Values:
• Integrity: Learners develop consistency as they engage in measuring the length of the chalkboard and the teacher’s table in metres.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Environmental awareness: Learners in groups measure the lengths of the 4 walls in their classroom and add the lengths.

Link to other learning areas: Learners relates measuring skills.

Suggested Learning resources:

● Books, pencils, rulers, sticks, bottles, metre rule, metre sticks, digital devices, strings
